bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Backed by the technological expertise and global legacy of the SKF Group, founded in 1907, which has operated in India since 1923
- Advanced manufacturing capabilities across facilities in India
- Well-established distribution network
- Long-standing customer relationships
- Five integrated technology-centric platforms enabling customised value-added solutions built on research-based innovation
- Technical Centre in Bengaluru serving as a dedicated hub for R&D and manufacturing excellence
- Access to the SKF Group's Technology Radar, open innovation platforms and sustained R&D investment

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and supply chain tensions — Global disruptions, trade restrictions and regional instability may affect supply chain continuity and input cost stability; mitigated through localisation, dual sourcing, inventory optimisation, digital supply chain solutions and a more regionalised operating model. The MD&A separately flags Middle East / Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea disruption, US-China tariff and technology restrictions, and volatile energy markets as pressures on an energy-importing economy such as India.
- Cost volatility — Fluctuations in raw material prices, energy costs and logistics expenses may impact profitability and operational planning; managed through pricing strategies, productivity improvement, cost optimisation programmes and flexible sourcing models.
- Information security and cybersecurity — As digitalisation accelerates, exposure to cybersecurity threats and data protection requirements has increased; addressed through investment in IT security infrastructure, employee awareness programmes and periodic security audits aligned with Group-wide data protection standards. A cybersecurity and data privacy framework and policy are in place, and no data privacy or cybersecurity consumer complaints were received in FY 2025-26 or the prior year.
- Technological change and innovation pace — Rapid advancements and evolving business models require continuous innovation to remain relevant; the Company leverages the SKF Group's Technology Radar, open innovation platforms and sustained R&D investment.
- Digitalisation and IT modernisation — Growing expectations for seamless customer experiences and integrated digital operations are accelerating digital transformation; addressed through strategic investment in digital capabilities, IT landscape simplification and targeted hiring of digital talent.
- Talent and leadership risk — Access to skilled talent in critical domains remains essential for sustaining innovation and operational excellence; addressed through leadership development, employee engagement, diversity and inclusion and strategic talent acquisition supporting succession planning.
- Climate and environmental impact — Climate change, water scarcity and evolving environmental regulations present operational and reputational exposure (the risk description is truncated in the source); the Company is advancing water neutrality initiatives, decarbonisation targets, renewable energy adoption and climate scenario risk assessments to prepare for future regulatory and environmental challenges.
- Post-demerger change in reporting boundary and procurement base — Following the demerger of the industrial business, the reporting boundary changed: intensity ratios and prior-year comparatives are not directly comparable, and MSME sourcing fell from 43% to 39% and district / neighbouring-district sourcing from 86.59% to 79% because previous-year figures included the subsequently demerged entity.

business.body: SKF India Limited operates as part of the Sweden-based SKF Group and represents the Group's automotive business in India, with a portfolio spanning bearings, seals, lubrication systems, mechatronics and reliability solutions. Historically the Company served both automotive and industrial applications; during FY 2025-26 the two businesses were demerged into separate entities and SKF India Limited now focuses exclusively on the automotive segment. Its core business is the manufacture of bearings and their components in India, offered through five technology-centric platforms and sold across both OEM and aftermarket channels.

outlook.body:
- Operate as a focused, independent automotive company post-demerger, building a world-class automotive business on application expertise, technological depth and durable customer relationships
- Strategically rebalance the automotive portfolio towards the evolving mobility landscape while strengthening presence across established vehicle segments, with advanced bearing solutions for passenger and commercial vehicles
- Sharpen focus on high-growth opportunities in the two-wheeler segment, with the Bengaluru Technical Centre as a dedicated hub for R&D and manufacturing excellence
- Expand EV capabilities across EV powertrains, unitized wheel-end systems and sensor-integrated solutions for next-generation mobility
- Continue investing in digitalisation, capacity enhancement and capability building to become a more agile, technology-led and customer-centric organisation
- Use participation in elite racing platforms as a high-performance laboratory to test and accelerate advanced technologies that cascade into mass-market EV platforms
- Strengthen supplier engagement through the Responsible Sourcing programme and accelerate supply-chain decarbonisation and renewable energy adoption with suppliers
- Leverage digitalisation and targeted network consolidation - advanced analytics, AI-driven route optimisation, IoT-enabled fleet monitoring and automated warehousing - to improve visibility, turnaround times and service reliability
- Build workforce capability for electrification, autonomous systems and digital manufacturing through the Leadership Accelerator Programme, SHE Leads and the global AI Ambassador Programme
- Operate the demerged automotive and industrial entities independently with distinct growth strategies, improved efficiency and strategic flexibility while both continue to leverage SKF's global technology ecosystem
- The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy, effective from 13th February 2017 and adopted under SEBI LODR, states the philosophy of enhancing stakeholder value and maximising shareholders' wealth from a long-term perspective, with returning cash to shareholders by way of dividends held to be an important component of overall shareholder value creation. The policy defines the internal and external factors, financial parameters, the treatment of retained earnings and the circumstances leading to declaration or non-declaration of dividend. Factors considered include reported net profit after tax available for distribution, accumulated profits brought forward from prior years available for distribution under the Companies Act 2013, the liquidity position and availability of free cash flows, and committed and projected cash-flow needs to finance forecasted capital expenditure, network expansion and working-capital requirements (the policy text is truncated in the source). Dividend is recommended by the Board in accordance with this policy and approved by shareholders at the AGM; the policy is hosted on the Company's website and forms Annexure-L to the Annual Report.
- Integrated EHS management system aligned with internationally recognised standards including ISO 45001, ISO 14001 and ISO 50001, with compliance assured through periodic audits, structured EHS performance tracking and defined governance forums
- Zero fatalities maintained during FY 2025-26 with continued improvement in key safety performance indicators, supported by a multi-year EHS culture transformation roadmap, safety culture pulse surveys, plant-level safety champions and expanded Safety Skill Centres with simulation-based training
- Sustainability agenda advanced through water neutrality initiatives, decarbonisation targets, renewable energy adoption and climate scenario risk assessments
- Comprehensive waste management framework built on waste minimisation, source segregation, resource recovery and responsible disposal, with non-hazardous waste routed through authorised recyclers and hazardous waste disposed, recycled, co-processed or recovered through authorised agencies; the Company also supports collection and recycling of post-consumer waste from its products and packaging
- Confirmed compliance with applicable Indian environmental laws including the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act and the Environment Protection Act and rules thereunder
- Input material sourcing in FY 2025-26: 39.00% directly from MSMEs / small producers and 79.00% from within the district and neighbouring districts
- 100% of turnover comes from products carrying information on environmental and social parameters relevant to the product, safe and responsible usage, and recycling and/or safe disposal
- Zero consumer complaints in FY 2025-26 across data privacy, advertising, cybersecurity, delivery of essential services, restrictive and unfair trade practices, and zero voluntary or forced product recalls on safety grounds
- Cyber security and data privacy framework and policy in place, with policies, controls and risk management processes to identify, monitor and mitigate cybersecurity risks
- CSR strategy integrated with core business strategy, with thrust areas of Education, Empowerment and Environment; the CSR Committee is chaired by the Managing Director with two-thirds independent directors and the total unspent CSR amount for FY 2025-26 is Nil
- Job creation disclosure for FY 2025-26 shows 4.81% of wage cost in semi-urban locations and 95.19% in metropolitan areas, on a post-demerger continuing-operations basis
- Affiliation with 10 trade and industry chambers / associations, including the Confederation of Indian Industry, National Safety Council and Quality Circle Forum of India
- Community grievance redressal mechanism including a dedicated address (socialconnect@skf.com) and feedback mechanisms at project locations and community engagement centres
- Assets insured against fire, riot, earthquake, terrorism and loss of profits, with product liability, public liability and directors' and officers' liability cover, and all employees covered against loss of life, hospitalisation and personal accident
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: SKF India serves the Indian automotive market from three manufacturing facilities, each described as part of the investment story the Company is building for the years ahead: Pune, Maharashtra - one of SKF India's oldest manufacturing hubs and a key facility for automotive and industrial bearing production; Bengaluru, Karnataka - a major bearing manufacturing plant and a critical part of the production network; and Haridwar, Uttarakhand - a strategic manufacturing site serving domestic automotive demand, included in the post-demerger investment (the sentence is cut off in the source). The Directors' Report states that the Company incurred a capital expenditure of INR 2,291.9 Million during the year. Manufacturing strategy is organised around four pillars - Lean, Green, Digital and People - with stated thrusts on capacity building for high-growth segments, sustainability through 'green' operations, regionalisation and localisation, technology step-up, assortment portfolio rationalisation (Factory PLP), and competency and leadership development. Initiatives undertaken in 2025-26 include an Industry 4.0 push with IIoT-enabled real-time machine monitoring and predictive maintenance, integrated Manufacturing Execution Systems with e-Kanban material flow and AI-based process optimisation, technological upgradation of existing grinding and assembly machines (groove grinding cycle time improved using Acoustic Emission technology from 2,000 pieces per hour to 2,400 pieces per hour), face grinding wheel development for hard rings cutting cycle time from 1.9 seconds to 1.6 seconds, a 20% reduction in non-productive time on bottleneck grinding machines, lean single-piece flow and conveyorised production cells, end-to-end in-house grinding, honing, assembly and laser marking capability, automated and AI-based vision inspection, and CMMS/SCADA/IIoT digital control rooms alongside energy-efficient technologies and heat recovery systems. Under BRSR Principle 2 the Company reports that 8.00% of capex in FY 2025-26 (5.00% in FY 2024-25) went into specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts, with R&D reported as Nil for both years.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian automotive industry remains optimistic about sustained growth across all vehicle categories in FY 2026-27, building on strong momentum in H2 FY 2025-26
- Outlook for the Indian automotive bearings industry in FY 2026-27 is positive, supported by steady growth across Passenger Vehicles, Two-Wheelers and Commercial Vehicles, with bearing demand closely aligned to automotive production trends
- Aftermarket expected to remain a key growth driver, supported by an expanding vehicle parc, ageing vehicles, rising utilisation, growth in organised aftermarket channels and preference for branded components; the aftermarket also provides stability when OE demand moderates and offers relatively stable value-added margins
- Increasing adoption of CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles expected to create additional opportunities for advanced, application-specific bearing solutions
- Electrification is a structural rather than cyclical shift, with EVs placing greater emphasis on low-friction, high-speed and noise-optimised bearings for electric drivetrains and wheel-end applications, requiring sustained investment in engineering, testing and application-specific solutions
- Broader technology trends - lightweighting, efficiency enhancement and predictive maintenance - are reshaping bearing demand, with OEMs prioritising precision-engineered solutions that reduce total cost of ownership
- Indian bearings market valued at around USD 5.2 Billion in 2025 and expected to grow to nearly USD 12.0 Billion by 2034, a CAGR of around 9.7% during 2026-2034
- Government programmes - PLI for automobiles and auto components, PM E-Drive, the Advanced Chemistry Cell battery initiative, the National Logistics Policy and Semicon India - accelerating investment, with localisation and import substitution encouraging domestic manufacture of critical components including bearings
- Regulatory transition through proposed BS VII norms and tighter CAFE standards reshaping automotive technologies
- FY 2025-26 performance supported by sustained demand across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and a resilient aftermarket, with performance partly impacted by one-off demerger-related expense
- Near-term risks flagged from the ongoing West Asia conflict - crude oil and commodity price volatility, currency fluctuations and disruptions in global shipping routes; a stable geopolitical environment and easing supply chain pressures seen as critical
- India real GDP growth for FY 2026-27 expected at 6.8-7.2%, with domestic demand, improving investment intentions and public infrastructure spending as primary growth drivers
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: SKF India posted 14.8% YoY revenue growth in Q4FY26 driven by strong OEM volumes, but PBT margins compressed to ~9% due to lapping of Q3 one-off gains and transitional demerger costs. Management guides for a sustainable 11-12% PBT margin in FY27 as capacity expansions (INR 500cr plan) reduce reliance on traded goods from the demerged industrial entity.

The Company intends to reach net zero by 2050, acting beyond its factories by driving supplier decarbonisation with low-carbon steel and renewables and cutting logistics emissions through smarter lanes, CNG vehicles and reduced air freight.

The Company is working towards net zero by 2050, including supplier decarbonisation with low-carbon steel and renewables and lower logistics emissions through smarter lanes, CNG vehicles and reduced air freight.
The Company is committed to achieving zero accidents across all SKF operations and reported an improvement versus the previous year.
Through optimised consumption, scaling reuse and improved recharge, the Company's sites are advancing water neutrality, aiming to return more to the environment than they consume.
The Company is expanding capabilities across EV powertrains, unitized wheel-end systems and sensor-integrated solutions, describing the EV space as its strongest momentum.

The Company is rebalancing its automotive portfolio and sharpening focus on high-growth opportunities, particularly the two-wheeler segment, with the Bengaluru Technical Centre as a dedicated R&D and manufacturing-excellence hub.

Following the FY 2025-26 demerger, SKF Automotive will concentrate on supporting India's evolving mobility ecosystem across EV, two-wheeler and wheel-end bearings segments while leveraging SKF's global technology ecosystem.

SKF Automotive will concentrate on supporting India's evolving mobility ecosystem across EV, two-wheeler and wheel-end bearings segments, operating with strategic autonomy while leveraging SKF's global technology ecosystem.

Each of the Company's three facilities - Pune, Bengaluru and Haridwar - is described as part of the investment programme being built for the years ahead, with Haridwar specifically included in the post-demerger investment.

The manufacturing strategy lists capacity building for high-growth segments, regionalisation and localisation, technology step-up and assortment portfolio rationalisation (Factory PLP) as stated priorities.
The Company is advancing towards Industry 4.0 through IIoT-enabled systems, integrated Manufacturing Execution Systems and AI-based analytics to enable predictive maintenance and consistent quality.

currentContext.expansion: SKF India serves the Indian automotive market from three manufacturing facilities, each described as part of the investment story the Company is building for the years ahead: Pune, Maharashtra - one of SKF India's oldest manufacturing hubs and a key facility for automotive and industrial bearing production; Bengaluru, Karnataka - a major bearing manufacturing plant and a critical part of the production network; and Haridwar, Uttarakhand - a strategic manufacturing site serving domestic automotive demand, included in the post-demerger investment (the sentence is cut off in the source). The Directors' Report states that the Company incurred a capital expenditure of INR 2,291.9 Million during the year. Manufacturing strategy is organised around four pillars - Lean, Green, Digital and People - with stated thrusts on capacity building for high-growth segments, sustainability through 'green' operations, regionalisation and localisation, technology step-up, assortment portfolio rationalisation (Factory PLP), and competency and leadership development. Initiatives undertaken in 2025-26 include an Industry 4.0 push with IIoT-enabled real-time machine monitoring and predictive maintenance, integrated Manufacturing Execution Systems with e-Kanban material flow and AI-based process optimisation, technological upgradation of existing grinding and assembly machines (groove grinding cycle time improved using Acoustic Emission technology from 2,000 pieces per hour to 2,400 pieces per hour), face grinding wheel development for hard rings cutting cycle time from 1.9 seconds to 1.6 seconds, a 20% reduction in non-productive time on bottleneck grinding machines, lean single-piece flow and conveyorised production cells, end-to-end in-house grinding, honing, assembly and laser marking capability, automated and AI-based vision inspection, and CMMS/SCADA/IIoT digital control rooms alongside energy-efficient technologies and heat recovery systems. Under BRSR Principle 2 the Company reports that 8.00% of capex in FY 2025-26 (5.00% in FY 2024-25) went into specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts, with R&D reported as Nil for both years.

risks.note: Global disruptions, trade restrictions and regional instability may affect supply chain continuity and input cost stability; mitigated through localisation, dual sourcing, inventory optimisation, digital supply chain solutions and a more regionalised operating model. The MD&A separately flags Middle East / Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea disruption, US-China tariff and technology restrictions, and volatile energy markets as pressures on an energy-importing economy such as India.

Fluctuations in raw material prices, energy costs and logistics expenses may impact profitability and operational planning; managed through pricing strategies, productivity improvement, cost optimisation programmes and flexible sourcing models.

As digitalisation accelerates, exposure to cybersecurity threats and data protection requirements has increased; addressed through investment in IT security infrastructure, employee awareness programmes and periodic security audits aligned with Group-wide data protection standards. A cybersecurity and data privacy framework and policy are in place, and no data privacy or cybersecurity consumer complaints were received in FY 2025-26 or the prior year.

Rapid advancements and evolving business models require continuous innovation to remain relevant; the Company leverages the SKF Group's Technology Radar, open innovation platforms and sustained R&D investment.

Growing expectations for seamless customer experiences and integrated digital operations are accelerating digital transformation; addressed through strategic investment in digital capabilities, IT landscape simplification and targeted hiring of digital talent.

Access to skilled talent in critical domains remains essential for sustaining innovation and operational excellence; addressed through leadership development, employee engagement, diversity and inclusion and strategic talent acquisition supporting succession planning.

Climate change, water scarcity and evolving environmental regulations present operational and reputational exposure (the risk description is truncated in the source); the Company is advancing water neutrality initiatives, decarbonisation targets, renewable energy adoption and climate scenario risk assessments to prepare for future regulatory and environmental challenges.

one-line thesis: SKF India posted 14.8% YoY revenue growth in Q4FY26 driven by strong OEM volumes, but PBT margins compressed to ~9% due to lapping of Q3 one-off gains and transitional demerger costs. Management guides for a sustainable 11-12% PBT margin in FY27 as capacity expansions (INR 500cr plan) reduce reliance on traded goods from the demerged industrial entity.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 5.55bn (Q4, +14.8% YoY), INR 20.3bn (FY26, +12.8% YoY); EBITDA Margin: ~15.3% (FY26, down from historical 16-17% due to mix/one-offs); PAT: Impacted by 770bps QoQ drop in PBT (to ~9%) due to lapping of Q3 forex/FD gains; Order Book: Visible till 2030 with strong EV wins; Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, Cash Flow INR 4.05bn (85% conversion). One-offs: Q3 had forex gains, FD interest, provision reversals; Q4/FY26 had minor demerger transition costs.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 6-8% CAGR expected; Margin: Sustainable PBT margin of 11-12% in near term (FY27); Order Inflow: Strong wins in EV motors and wheel hubs; Capex: INR 200cr in FY27, part of INR 500cr plan (FY26-28).
order book & pipeline: Strong portfolio of wins across 2W, PV, CV extending to 2030; Specific new launches in EV motor bearings and wheel hub bearings for FY27.
segment / subsidiary detail: OEM contributes ~66% of sales (+20% YoY); Distribution ~20% (slight decline); Exports ~8%; Industrial share ~6%. 2-Wheeler is dominant volume contributor. Top 5 customers ~50%, Top 10 ~70% (Bajaj, Mahindra, Tata key).
growth verticals / optionality: White spaces in unitized bearings for SCV/LCV and low-friction transmissions for CAFE-3 norms; EV adoption (currently 6% of 2W, 4% of PV) offering higher value-per-product despite lower bearing count.
margins & cost dynamics: Margin compression due to OEM mix shift (lower margin vs aftermarket), raw material inflation (steel) with lagged pass-through, and transitional trading from Industrial entity. Sustainable PBT guided at 11-12%.
capex / expansion: INR 500cr planned over FY26-28; INR 200cr allocated for FY27. Focus on new lines in Haridwar and Pune to increase localization and reduce trading.
capital allocation: Focus on capacity expansion to capture organic growth; working capital normalized after Q4 spike; no specific dividend/buyback commentary.
risks & watch-items: Raw material price inflation (steel) with pass-through lags; Slower-than-expected EV adoption rates; Customer concentration (Top 10 = 70%); Transitional dependency on demerged Industrial entity for traded goods.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic on volume growth but defensive on margin compression; committed to transparency post-feedback; emphasizes 'quality of earnings' and cash flow over pure top-line growth.
non-obvious takeaways: Reverse carve-out structure: SKF India Ltd retained Auto business while Industrial demerged; currently renting land/assets to Industrial entity; high traded goods volume is temporary bridge until new auto-capacity comes online; EV bearings command multifold pricing despite lower unit count.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: SKF India Limited is the SKF Group's automotive business in India, delivering high-precision bearings and engineering solutions to vehicle OEMs and the aftermarket after demerging its industrial business in FY 2025-26.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: SKF India Limited operates as part of the Sweden-based SKF Group and represents the Group's automotive business in India, with a portfolio spanning bearings, seals, lubrication systems, mechatronics and reliability solutions. Historically the Company served both automotive and industrial applications; during FY 2025-26 the two businesses were demerged into separate entities and SKF India Limited now focuses exclusively on the automotive segment. Its core business is the manufacture of bearings and their components in India, offered through five technology-centric platforms and sold across both OEM and aftermarket channels.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian automotive industry remains optimistic about sustained growth across all vehicle categories in FY 2026-27, building on strong momentum in H2 FY 2025-26
- Outlook for the Indian automotive bearings industry in FY 2026-27 is positive, supported by steady growth across Passenger Vehicles, Two-Wheelers and Commercial Vehicles, with bearing demand closely aligned to automotive production trends
- Aftermarket expected to remain a key growth driver, supported by an expanding vehicle parc, ageing vehicles, rising utilisation, growth in organised aftermarket channels and preference for branded components; the aftermarket also provides stability when OE demand moderates and offers relatively stable value-added margins
- Increasing adoption of CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles expected to create additional opportunities for advanced, application-specific bearing solutions
- Electrification is a structural rather than cyclical shift, with EVs placing greater emphasis on low-friction, high-speed and noise-optimised bearings for electric drivetrains and wheel-end applications, requiring sustained investment in engineering, testing and application-specific solutions
- Broader technology trends - lightweighting, efficiency enhancement and predictive maintenance - are reshaping bearing demand, with OEMs prioritising precision-engineered solutions that reduce total cost of ownership
- Indian bearings market valued at around USD 5.2 Billion in 2025 and expected to grow to nearly USD 12.0 Billion by 2034, a CAGR of around 9.7% during 2026-2034
- Government programmes - PLI for automobiles and auto components, PM E-Drive, the Advanced Chemistry Cell battery initiative, the National Logistics Policy and Semicon India - accelerating investment, with localisation and import substitution encouraging domestic manufacture of critical components including bearings
- Regulatory transition through proposed BS VII norms and tighter CAFE standards reshaping automotive technologies
- FY 2025-26 performance supported by sustained demand across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and a resilient aftermarket, with performance partly impacted by one-off demerger-related expense
- Near-term risks flagged from the ongoing West Asia conflict - crude oil and commodity price volatility, currency fluctuations and disruptions in global shipping routes; a stable geopolitical environment and easing supply chain pressures seen as critical
- India real GDP growth for FY 2026-27 expected at 6.8-7.2%, with domestic demand, improving investment intentions and public infrastructure spending as primary growth drivers

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margin compression due to OEM mix shift (lower margin vs aftermarket), raw material inflation (steel) with lagged pass-through, and transitional trading from Industrial entity. Sustainable PBT guided at 11-12%.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Focus on capacity expansion to capture organic growth; working capital normalized after Q4 spike; no specific dividend/buyback commentary.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: SKF India serves the Indian automotive market from three manufacturing facilities, each described as part of the investment story the Company is building for the years ahead: Pune, Maharashtra - one of SKF India's oldest manufacturing hubs and a key facility for automotive and industrial bearing production; Bengaluru, Karnataka - a major bearing manufacturing plant and a critical part of the production network; and Haridwar, Uttarakhand - a strategic manufacturing site serving domestic automotive demand, included in the post-demerger investment (the sentence is cut off in the source). The Directors' Report states that the Company incurred a capital expenditure of INR 2,291.9 Million during the year. Manufacturing strategy is organised around four pillars - Lean, Green, Digital and People - with stated thrusts on capacity building for high-growth segments, sustainability through 'green' operations, regionalisation and localisation, technology step-up, assortment portfolio rationalisation (Factory PLP), and competency and leadership development. Initiatives undertaken in 2025-26 include an Industry 4.0 push with IIoT-enabled real-time machine monitoring and predictive maintenance, integrated Manufacturing Execution Systems with e-Kanban material flow and AI-based process optimisation, technological upgradation of existing grinding and assembly machines (groove grinding cycle time improved using Acoustic Emission technology from 2,000 pieces per hour to 2,400 pieces per hour), face grinding wheel development for hard rings cutting cycle time from 1.9 seconds to 1.6 seconds, a 20% reduction in non-productive time on bottleneck grinding machines, lean single-piece flow and conveyorised production cells, end-to-end in-house grinding, honing, assembly and laser marking capability, automated and AI-based vision inspection, and CMMS/SCADA/IIoT digital control rooms alongside energy-efficient technologies and heat recovery systems. Under BRSR Principle 2 the Company reports that 8.00% of capex in FY 2025-26 (5.00% in FY 2024-25) went into specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts, with R&D reported as Nil for both years.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic on volume growth but defensive on margin compression; committed to transparency post-feedback; emphasizes 'quality of earnings' and cash flow over pure top-line growth.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Backed by the technological expertise and global legacy of the SKF Group, founded in 1907, which has operated in India since 1923
- Advanced manufacturing capabilities across facilities in India
- Well-established distribution network
- Long-standing customer relationships
- Five integrated technology-centric platforms enabling customised value-added solutions built on research-based innovation
- Technical Centre in Bengaluru serving as a dedicated hub for R&D and manufacturing excellence
- Access to the SKF Group's Technology Radar, open innovation platforms and sustained R&D investment
- Participation in elite racing platforms used as a high-performance laboratory whose material and engineering insights cascade into mass-market EV platforms
- Enhanced testing and validation capabilities supporting conventional, electric and emerging mobility platforms

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material price inflation (steel) with pass-through lags; Slower-than-expected EV adoption rates; Customer concentration (Top 10 = 70%); Transitional dependency on demerged Industrial entity for traded goods.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Reverse carve-out structure: SKF India Ltd retained Auto business while Industrial demerged; currently renting land/assets to Industrial entity; high traded goods volume is temporary bridge until new auto-capacity comes online; EV bearings command multifold pricing despite lower unit count.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Operate as a focused, independent automotive company post-demerger, building a world-class automotive business on application expertise, technological depth and durable customer relationships
- Strategically rebalance the automotive portfolio towards the evolving mobility landscape while strengthening presence across established vehicle segments, with advanced bearing solutions for passenger and commercial vehicles
- Sharpen focus on high-growth opportunities in the two-wheeler segment, with the Bengaluru Technical Centre as a dedicated hub for R&D and manufacturing excellence
- Expand EV …
